reported_success.location: p. 63, section 4.5.3, interpretation following regression results
reported_success.quote:
These results suggest that anxiety experienced at the processing stage has a more
significant effect on general language anxiety than anxiety experienced at the output
stage of language learning, which is also consistent with Onwuegbuzie et al.’s (2000)
findings.

notes: Original side is an unassigned placeholder, not assessed. No mapping from audit ID or row order to predictors was attempted. Printed p. 63 candidates: input β = 0.18, t = 2.42, p < 0.05; process β = 0.43, t = 5.32, p < 0.01; output β = 0.31, t = 4.31, p < 0.01. Coefficients are labelled beta/β; this paragraph does not explicitly identify their standardisation, so requested standardized-metric identity is not assumed. The omnibus model prints adjusted R2 = 0.62, F(3,129) = 73.90, p < 0.01; these are not substituted for a predictor coefficient. Recruitment/current-study N = 134 is explicitly reported, also for factor analyses/correlations, but is not explicitly the analytic N of the p. 63 regression. No N derived from degrees of freedom or unrelated group counts. Reported success is the authors’ shared narrative comparison for this regression, not a resolved audit-row-to-predictor mapping. PDF printed p. 63 visually checked against canonical text.
